entry.title: The Complete Manual of Instigation
entry.content:
The Complete Manual of Instigation

Notes from the Night of Nov. 20

We must distinguish the nature of a madman’s act of burning down his own house—just as Schopenhauer distinguishes starvation from ordinary suicide—from the act of calmly burning down one’s own house out of absolute reason. First, we shall demonstrate the correctness of this rational act, which I have wrested from Schopenhauer’s grasp. What will subsequently be discovered is the absolute rationality of this action.
Schopenhauer overlooked the other side of suicide, namely, the reverse manifestation of the negation of the will. Even though he mentioned in passing, "yet they still feel guilt when indulging in harmless pleasures.“ What Schopenhauer still overlooked is the emergence of the other side of the negation of the will. Not every act that alleviates suffering is an affirmation of the will, for there clearly exist more painful and prolonged methods of suicide than starvation—such as subjecting oneself to the death of a thousand cuts while starving? These means of amplifying suffering are precisely what Schopenhauer so lavishly praised. That historian ought to have gouged out his own eyes, for the eyes, as the finest weapon of cognition, need to be destroyed by cognition itself—or rather, this is the self-sublation of cognition, much like a valiant warrior severing his own wrist. Only thus could it be proven that cognition itself is powerful enough to annul volition. And thereby sanctify oneself all the more. Furthermore, ought he not to have committed suicide while seated before a feast of dainties from land and sea? Otherwise, it is difficult to say whether it was merely objective conditions that led to his death by starvation; before the moment his cognition could annul the will, he prematurely, passively, met a painful death—perhaps he wished to eat, yet found himself in a desolate wilderness, a place unsought by man for a month, with nothing at all to consume. Thus, his sacred starvation degenerates into what Schopenhauer views as a madman’s act of taking poison, the impurity of a slow death. From the above, one can see just how inadequate this example cited by Schopenhauer truly is. This will further illustrate the non-existence of Schopenhauer’s transcendental change—that is, its lack of empirical existence—thereby arguing in favor of my own view on suicide.
Another point I have long wanted to gripe about (since I cannot find the book right now, I am quoting from my own vivid memory) is: ”They (the ascetics) may plunge from snowy mountains or be crushed beneath the wheels of a carriage out of an extreme negation of the will. This too is their asceticism“ versus what he says in Chapter 67: ”Nothing approaches the negation of the will more closely than this special manner of suicide, starvation. It is as though, while he starves, some noble voice is guiding him.“ This is truly baffling. Why, sir, do you not condemn those monks who did not starve themselves, but instead committed suicide prematurely, through ordinary acts that shortened their suffering? You ought not to praise them. Unless, deep within your heart, you were aware of the inadequacy of your own theory, and a psychological movement akin to Kant’s took place within you, thereby exposing the flaws of your theory. Schopenhauer accepts only starvation, yet lavishly praises plunging off a cliff; this is a direct manifestation of Schopenhauer’s contradiction. Indirectly, it manifests in the impurity of the details of these acts, such as that historian—he actually ate something.
We arrive at the conclusion:
Schopenhauer failed to provide any realistic account of the ideal transcendental change. His irresponsibility and self-contradiction are embodied in Section 67. Like saintly virtue, that which utterly renounces the mundane and cannot be acquired a posteriori does not exist within this world.
Here, Schopenhauer’s restrictions on suicide fly right out of this world.

Since transcendental change, like saintly virtue, cannot be subjectively acquired, it does not exist within the world, for everything within the world can be acquired—that is to say, can be spoken of. Therefore, this means that even passively accepting a transcendental change that suddenly flies over to you becomes—just as the reader feels when reading this for the first time—something utterly abstruse, a mystery of mysteries. The existence of saints is not one in ten million, but zero.
Here, after Schopenhauer’s death, I begin my inquiry into rational suicide. First, it is worth emphasizing that negation is an absolute value of the will. In moments of happiness—which is to say, when volition manifests just as wildly, as it is being continuously satisfied—this too is a fine opportunity to slay volition. Unlike the commonly held distinction between “laying down the butcher’s cleaver to attain Buddhahood on the spot” and enduring “the nine-times-nine eighty-one tribulations,” I believe that a good man is already a Buddha. What remains for him to do, the eighty-one tribulations he undergoes, is on the contrary a meaningless business of agitating volition. Those eighty-one tribulations are, instead, just like food, something worthy of guilt. Because the negation of volition is fundamentally an absolute value rather than a numerical one. Attempting to train oneself not to fear suffering, and to crave suffering as if it were life itself, still 【cannot turn suffering into something beloved】; all of this is meaningless, a reverse agitation of volition. The suffering thus obtained is likewise meaningless, utterly incapable of curbing volition again. In the positive direction lies fine food; their absolute values are fundamentally identical.
We need do nothing extra; under rational conditions, so long as we calmly go to meet death, we achieve the success of Lincord. He was not perfect. Perfection, in this world or within the world, within our sphere, does not exist. Thus, 【after bringing Historian Lin down (from atop Schopenhauer’s head)】, we possess the opportunity (the right) to sit as equals with him.
My notes, in a small part, suffer from a profound confusion of thought, making it difficult to express within those few words, much like Kant’s. They require copious annotations, especially for the purpose of supplementation and explanation, I suppose.

Notes from the Morning of Nov. 21

As an attempt to violently destroy volition, contraception, in Schopenhauer’s view, is just like what he calls phenomenon-destroying suicide: entirely an exercise in futility. Volition exists outside the individual, yet does it exist within the individual? Schopenhauer did not offer further refutations regarding methods of contraception, an attempt akin to ordinary suicide. Because here, he could not make an explicitly stated explanation that violates logic. Regarding suicide, perhaps it is difficult for us to discuss. However, regarding methods of contraception, we can state with absolute certainty—contraception is unequivocally effective; so long as we wish it, we can, in this one-off act, avoid the consequences of failing to practice asceticism—provided the condom meets quality standards. Which is to say, the effectiveness of this rudimentary method of contraception thoroughly and completely proves the effectiveness of suicide. How perfect. The objective is effective; the objective is a means to assist our asceticism. For instance, the objective impossibility of satisfaction can assist in the arousal of our reason—is this not asceticism? That is the first point; second, this objectively restricts the manifestation of action, namely, knowing something is unfeasible and thus refraining from doing it. Only manifestation is volition.

Notes from Nov. 22

Only the existence of natural law can ensure the logical existence of the future.
There is no necessity for a past life to exist; we cannot explain our own origins, our own birth. Even if a past life existed, that would be a higher-level “I,” just as after this phenomenon of “I” dies, the higher-level “I” does not die. As a phenomenon, “I” can explain nothing at all. The higher level here does not refer to “humanity”—taken literally, humanity will undoubtedly go extinct as well. Thus, the teacher’s explanation of Su Shi’s line, “If we behold them from that which changeth not, then neither the myriad things nor I shall ever know an end,” is nothing more than a postponement of death, failing to solve the problem at its root. Because that is contradictory.
My purpose is to demonstrate how to commit suicide so as to be happier after death.
I am nearly a cult, nearly anti-human. Yet my theory is grounded in humanism; everything is for man, for the human individual, rather than the happiness of humanity as a whole—abandoning the individual for the sake of the whole is something only socialism would do. Therefore, in my view, suicide as a practice of transferring suffering is also permitted—because the suffering is not inflicted by the suicide at all, but generated spontaneously by yourself; the one who commits suicide has merely defended his life completely, and the right to suicide is the true embodiment of valuing life.

Notes from Nov. 23

entry.title: A night swept away by the autumn wind
The Secret of the Clock House
entry.content:
Once upon a time, there was a little blue river, winding like a ribbon around a vast green forest.
Once upon a time, there was a vast green forest, guarding that cabin in the very center, the witch’s cabin made of wood.
Once upon a time, there was a white-haired witch, she lived within the green forest, and she wore black earrings engraved with a golden sun and moon, upon which were etched fine inscriptions.

The witch wore a cloak and magical robes crafted from the wings of that giant dragon in the mountains, carrying the deep black of midnight and the dark blue of a sinking moon, as well as the dragonkin’s power to soar. They were dotted with tiny specks of light, just like stars flickering in the dark night.

The witch always wove through the tall trees like the wind, she was searching for prey, namely those uninvited humans who crossed the river to trespass into her territory, and she was also searching for her companions, her darlings–the cats that could sprout up anywhere throughout the forest.
She remembered that just yesterday, at the back of a black stone, in the shadow of the penny ferns, beside the shallow stream, upon the damp bank, she had found a brownish-yellow kitten, curled up into a tiny ball, its body rising and falling with each faint breath.
The witch carefully gathered the kitten into her pouch, the other side of the pouch led to a cat paradise of her own making, where there were countless adorable kittens, though that place was quite some distance from here.
The witch soon found the uninvited visitor, it was a frail little girl, crying and shouting as she stumbled deep into the forest.
The little girl had come to this forest with her father’s boat, and after her father died in an accident, she was left all alone.

The witch cut off the little girl’s head, and buried it together with her father’s head.

entry.title: Yi'an's Childhood
entry.content:
Begin

Yi’an lived with his grandparents throughout elementary school.
On that day in first grade, I first met my grandparents and saw the house I would live in for the next seven years, the photos my memory took are all golden, no houses had been built on the open ground in front of Grandma’s door yet, it was patches and patches of green, with mulberry leaves I needed to feed my silkworms, all green plants. Later reinforced concrete gradually appeared there, later the green plants suddenly disappeared, and even later big houses suddenly sprang up from the ground, the open space originally full of sunlight became tall gray brick walls.

Behind Grandma’s house was a huge bamboo forest, I still clearly remember to this day, when a gust of wind blew, the tops of the tall bamboo swayed wildly and rustled in the wind, as if they were about to be snapped by the wind, that bamboo must have been six stories high, inside the bamboo forest were a few chickens raised by Grandma, and occasionally stray cats would appear. Many families lived behind the bamboo forest, a female classmate from elementary school lived in the village behind my house.

In elementary school I seemed to interact more closely with female classmates, YYH and CMT always came to my house to play during elementary school, we played dominoes, I would set up a full circle brimming on the dining table in the living room, and then take a video watching them stumble and fall one by one, the video is of course long gone (laughs). Aside from dominoes, they were both good at playing poker, even at nine o’clock they would occasionally come to my house to play, we sat on different sides of the living room dining table, playing muddled card games.
YYH and WSN rode my grandpa’s tricycle home every day, but as we got into higher grades, Grandpa inevitably found his strength falling short of his wishes. I still remember the day before W passed away, at the school gate, seeing them run quickly toward Grandpa’s tricycle made me feel so bad that I cried out and angrily scolded them. Later on the road, WSN apologetically handed me a leaf to say sorry. The next morning, I heard classmates in the classroom saying that WSN got into a car accident. Her relatives concluded the cause of the accident was W’s grandma being obsessed with playing mahjong, giving WSN money to go buy breakfast by herself, and WSN got into the accident on her way to school alone. A classmate said she saw brains spilled all over the ground.
My dear Nannan. A few days after I heard about it, a classmate mentioned her during the speech under the national flag.

Around first or second grade I went to CMT’s house to play once, Ori-Princess, we happily watched it together in her room. Afterward we played role-play as a queen and a bandit, of course she was the queen, and later she bizarrely took off her clothes and only used a quilt as a cape, , while the role I played was something like a lustful bandit. What an innocent childhood indeed.

In fifth grade, my deskmate XSY, his decision not to participate in the play required by the teacher shocked me at the time, and makes me agree wholeheartedly now. At the time he was just always reading, always reading, always reading, in my memory he seemed to always be lying on his desk with his head down reading. Later he transferred schools and left. I heard ZSY say she had a book she hadn’t returned to X yet, but it seemed she couldn’t return it anymore either.

ZSY was a cute girl, from second grade to fifth grade, we would go together to our math teacher’s house for tutoring. What still leaves a deep impression on me is that she and I shared an umbrella on a certain rainy day, “Hey, Surname M”, she always liked to call me that. She had a pretty big birthmark on her face. I suspect she liked me

Rainy

Rainy is the girl I like. Rainy’s figure seemed a bit taller than other girls her age. Rainy is very cute, Rainy is as cute as a kitten, Rainy is also very cute when she smiles. Rainy likes anime and manga, Rainy already liked anime and manga back in elementary school, when Rainy started seventh grade, she brought a lot of Fujiya lollipops. Rainy is an introverted girl.
In seventh grade, at two o’clock in the afternoon on September twenty-fifth, two thousand and sixteen, through anonymous messages, I confessed my feelings to Rainy after my identity was almost seen through.
Rainy said she had also liked me for a long time in elementary school, Rainy said the time she liked me was definitely longer than the time I liked her. Rainy said she already knew long ago that she liked me, though if that was the case why did she still make me confess first. Rainy’s birthday is April nineteenth. Rainy was in Class 2, while I was in Class 4. After moving up to high school, Rainy was still in the same school as me, but still in different classes.
If only she and I were in the same class, that would have been great.
Irrationally, I broke up with Rainy on January eighth of the following year. Go marry the 2D world you like, the exact words on QQ.
Of course I regretted it to death.

However, later, in eighth grade, RJW, Rainy’s friend told me, once when Rainy’s homeroom teacher was investigating if any students in the class were dating, R said, she watched a blushing Rainy say that she was dating me, her face was really so, so red, R said with a grin like that.
After that, every time at the cafeteria entrance, if I saw Rainy walking together with a few of her good friends, they would laugh and call out Rainy’s name at me, they were really so gossipy. Though I didn’t show any reaction, I was really happy in my heart. Once the short-sleeved school uniform Rainy wore was very baggy, though it was black. Rainy was always very quiet, she always spoke in a very low voice, always only talking to the people right next to her.

Later I tried to re-add Rainy’s QQ many times, but I was either rejected, and the only time it went through after revealing my identity, I was chewed out by her. She sent me a meme of backing away at the speed of light.

In high school, I saw Rainy a few times, she is still so cute. Rainy is still the same as in middle school, the same as in elementary school. But I didn’t dare go up and talk to her, even though she was right beside me.

Later on QQ, RJW said Rainy’s feelings for me were already a thing of childhood, it was in the past, and there was no need to do anything anymore. I don’t really agree with that.
But I still like her so much, just looking at her makes me so, so satisfied.

Xin

Xin was my middle school class monitor. In ninth grade, she took a leave of absence and dropped back to eighth grade. Although the teacher never told us explicitly, the classmates all seemed to know that Xin had depression. At least it seemed to have an unknown cause just like mine. Xin was an excellent class monitor, both classmates and teachers evaluated her as such, she was the pillar of our class. Xin seemed to have once tried to jump off the building in the dorm, but was stopped by the homeroom teacher. Xin seemed to have fainted on the playground once. I remember one time, maybe during evening self-study, Xin’s mother came to pick Xin up to go home with an anxious look on her face, and Xin’s condition in my memory seemed describable as somatized unconsciousness. Xin once had an episode during the Chinese teacher’s class, the cause looking just as unknown as mine, Xin forcefully kicked her desk at the time, startling the whole class, the Chinese teacher was quite calm though, saying that even if she tore up her books, it had nothing to do with him.
Xin once sat behind me, that time was an awards ceremony for the midterm exams, I got a prize, a light brown plastic doll. Xin said she wanted it, but at the time I thought it was very cute and wanted to save it for my mom, although I didn’t give it to my mom later either. Xin angrily told others behind me that I must have gotten a girlfriend, and that was why I wouldn’t give that cute doll to her. If it were now, I would definitely give it to her.

In ninth grade I fell in love with pens, it was another awards ceremony, in the big classroom, I got a long blue pen with a pendant, the barrel had a cute white bear pattern, and it was even 3D. I examined that pen with such utmost seriousness that my classmates all thought I was weird.

In middle school there were two girls, why is it girls again, during that time, before exams, they would always strike a pos together to cheer me on! I was really so happy, back at that time. Later when we went to high school, they still hung out together all the time, they said they hoped I would come hang out with them.
My deskmate in middle school was a very pretty girl, she could do voice acting, and seemed to use it often when talking to teachers, a girl’s voice is already very sweet, and after being optimized by her you can’t imagine how nice it sounded. Her hair was styled very nicely. Once she asked me if it was better to tie her ponytail high or low, although I had a detailed answer in my heart, tying it low looks quieter with the gentle and elegant feel of an ancient girl tying it high looks very lively it still depends on what type you want to show though many girls in the class tie it high and you often tie it high too so why not try tying it low this time, however, what came out of my mouth was, both look good. She was extremely angry, then that’s the same as saying nothing at all.

Music exams in middle school were different from elementary school, though elementary school seemed to have no music exams at all. I was forced to go on stage and sing a song, back then I was listening to Jay Chou, and now several years later I am still listening to Jay Chou. Back then classmates in the dorm would often sing all kinds of songs, the sky of celadon awaits the misty rain, the haze of smoke lingers o’er the stone-grill shop, boohoo I can’t really remember the others.
I sang Blue and White Porcelain, because I was introverted, it seemed to be the first time many classmates had ever heard my voice, and the whole room applauded.
Later, there was another music exam, I sang Far Away, I carefully studied how to sing the Rap part but ended up only singing the beginning, and the result was not optimistic either, I cry.
There was a girl in the class, Yi sang Common Jasmine Orange.

My high school experience is black.

I lost the happiness of elementary and middle school. But who knows if elementary and middle school were really as happy as I think, in middle school I even had urinary incontinence in public during self-study class because I held my pee for too long, which was obviously not good at all.
So, it seems my life will never get better. Unless I die.
